newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. Commerce Secretary Daley visits Canada.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Commerce Secretary Daley visits Canada.

text.p: The salmon fishing dispute between Canada and the United States will not hurt trade relations between the two countries, U.S. Secretary of Commerce William Daley said on Monday.
"This problem will not go to the heart of our relationship. It cannot be allowed to do that," Daley told reporters in Montreal on the first day of a three-day trade mission to Canada.

In a speech to a Montreal business group, Daley said he was confident the salmon dispute would be resolved as successfully as other contentious issues such as Canadian softwood lumber exports to the United States.
But he said the solution in the salmon dispute would have to come from the fishermen involved on both sides of the border.
"This is only going to be solved if the stakeholders solve it, not the governments," he said.
Daley said he was hopeful that special envoys appointed by both countries would be able to "jump-start" negotiations when they resume this fall.
William Ruckelshaus, former head of the Environmental Protection Agency, will lead U.S. efforts. University of British Columbia President and Chancellor David Strangway is the Canadian envoy.

The dispute flared in late July when Canadian fishermen blockaded an Alaska state ferry in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, for three days to protest against alleged overfishing by Americans of salmon returning from the ocean to inland Canadian waters where they spawned. The United States denies overfishing.
Daley cited the $1 billion in daily two-way trade between Canada and the United States as proof of their strong trading relationship.

During his mission, Daley will focus on trade opportunities for small and medium-sized businesses. On Tuesday, Daley is scheduled to meet with separatist Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard before going to Ottawa for talks with Canada's international trade and industry ministers.
Daley's mission ends in Toronto on Wednesday, but he also had a one-day visit to Vancouver scheduled for Thursday.
